question: Which of the following is a precipitation reaction?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CuSO4 (aq) + BaCl2 (aq) → BaSO4 (s) + CuCl2 (aq)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CuSO4 (aq) + BaCl2 (aq) → BaSO4 (s) + CuCl2 (aq)** is a precipitation reaction.
 
• In a precipitation reaction, two aqueous solutions react to form an insoluble solid called a precipitate.
 
• Here, when copper(II) sulfate solution reacts with barium chloride solution, barium sulfate, which is insoluble in water, precipitates out.
 
• The other product, copper(II) chloride, remains in the aqueous phase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Precipitation reactions are a type of double displacement reaction where an insoluble salt is formed as a product.
 
• These reactions are commonly used in various chemical analyses and separations.
 
• The formation of a precipitate can be used to identify the presence of specific ions in a solution.
 
• Other examples of precipitation reactions include the reaction between silver nitrate and sodium chloride to form silver chloride precipitate.
 
• Precipitation reactions are important in fields such as analytical chemistry, environmental science, and materials science.
